drive_against_action_json.note: the bore state used here against the numbers printed in action/action.json (same model, re-run through action/sim.py ib_solve with the stored calibration)

literature.note: model against published rifle measurements. The published rifle is a 7.62 mm (M14 class), not this one, so agreement to about 10 % is the most these can show.

temperatures_K.what: primary flash, next to the muzzle
temperatures_K.status: prediction: the temperature is action/'s reservoir temperature at exit, nothing fitted here

temperatures_K.what: intermediate flash, behind the Mach disc
temperatures_K.source: Klingenberg & Mach 1976 (Na and K line reversal, 100 to 300 mm from the muzzle)
temperatures_K.status: onset is a prediction; the 300 K rise is taken from this same paper, so the peak is not independent

temperatures_K.what: gas in the intermediate flash region late in the event
temperatures_K.published: 1468 K at 0.70 ms falling to about 500 K at 1.53 ms
temperatures_K.source: CARS temperature measurements in the muzzle flash region of a 7.62 mm rifle (DTIC ADA190786)
temperatures_K.status: mismatch late: the model keeps the shocked gas at the reservoir temperature and has no mixing with cold air, so it stays far too hot after about 1 ms (it has stopped glowing by then: glow_floor). The time origin of the published figures was not confirmed.

mach_disc.note: two published correlations for the Mach disc of a steady under-expanded jet, fed with action/'s exit pressure: x/D = 0.69 M sqrt(gamma p_e/p_inf) (Lewis & Carlson 1964) and x/D = 0.67 sqrt(p_0/p_inf) (Ashkenas & Sherman 1966). They differ by 16 %, which is the uncertainty of the jet model before any hider. The muzzle jet never reaches the steady value: the pressure has fallen by the time the disc is established.

light_meter.status: calibration, not a check: one factor (0.0981) on all thermal light makes the 16 in / 5-slot run read 0.48 lx; the secondary peak is set by the bare-muzzle reading. Before calibration the thermal model is 10 times too bright.
